Y precisamente es la América Latina la región del mundo la más a propósito para el desarrollo de este nuevo Estado de tipo industrializado y libre. Después, es claro, de la misma manera que el soldado es sustituido por el hombre de ley y el hombre de ley es sustituido por el técnico, venará el período del gobierno de los filósofos. La educación será entonces la tarea fundamental; ya no. la producción, convertida en organismo en marcha, sino la tarea de cultivar y desenvolver los espíritus. Pero el gobierno de los filósofos, si su misión no se corrompe, tendrá que llevarnos a otro grado todavía superior del progreso social, a la desaparición del Estado que también es medio y no fin; pues no hay otro fin que el individuo, la chispa divina, el Alma y Dios, y todo lo demás es como paja y vanidad. Al desaparecer por innecesario el Estado, la última huella de la barbarie también se irá con él y las formas todas del nacionalismo serán cosa del pasado.[¶ 30] Tenemos, pues, cinco períodos en los procesos del go-, bierno, cinco tipos de gobernante; el soldado, el abogado [p. 24.1] el ingeniero, el filósoto y el período que tendremos que llamar anarquista que propiamente es el definitivo. Pero nos hallamos en la actualidad, en la época en que todos los soldados deben ponerse a obedecer al hombre que hace lasleyes y en la que todos, más o menos, debemos trabajar como ingenieros y como constructores. Hay tanto desperdicio, tanta incapacidad, tanta necesidad sin satisfacción en el mundo contemporáneo que se hace indispensable que el período del ingeniero se anticipe y se adelante. Trabajo y producción es el lema salvador; pero trabajo y producción para beneficio de todos los que trabajan, sin distinción de clase ni de color. Todos los demás propósitos pueden esperar. Nuestra civilización será un fracaso mientras siga produciendo, como las especies inferiores, gentes y más gentes, pero sin medios de alimentarlas y educarlas. Cuidemos de que en la América nuestra no se recaiga en los mismos errores. Necesitamos emigración, pero sin olvidar que antes que muchos niños, necesitamos escuelas para los niños que ya han nacido. Una de las causas fundamentales de que la civilización no prospere, se encuentra en el hecho de que las poblaciones inferiores se reproducen con exceso y desbordan sobre las más avanzadas que naturalmente reducen su prole. Por eso la civilización sólo se sentirá garantizada así que la cultura y la verdadera moralidad, que supone la responsabilidad, se propaguen en todoslos grupos. Mientras la civilización siga siendo en mayor o menor grado un asunto nacional, no habrá esperanza de que ocurran cambios radicales en la historia del mundo. Las invasiones y las conquistas seguirán produciendo otros tantos medioevos; pues mientras halla nacionalismos habrá imperialismos y afán de conquistas; es decir medioevalismo y barbarie. Al reves de todo esto, la civilización quiere decir universalidad, conciencia y fraternidad.
e: Perhaps the most urgent need of our continent is the possession of the scientific technology105 that will position us to harness our resources (possibly the only effective contribution of modern times). For this particular end,106 we need contributions from Europeans,107 as well as from the engineers and technicians108 of North America.As for social and spiritual life, Latin America has already begun to follow its own path. It has the right to its own thought, just as you have the right to yours. Fortunately, this autonomy is not a cause for discord. Thought belongs to no one. It is a common treasure. In philosophy, art, and social matters, we will take examples from the entire world, in accordance with our own judgment and with the end of building better. Send, then, your artists and thinkers to Latin America. Their seeds will bear fruit, though the fruits will inevitably appear more or less transformed. Latin America is no longer a field of unlimited proselytism. Though our capacity for assimilation remains great, we have begun to produce and think for ourselves. But you, and all people, will have the opportunity to influence the character of our intellectual creations. Send us your ideas, but above all, send Latin America your technology,109 your engineers, and your builders. At first, it will be necessary for you to support them from Europe, in the form of supplying tools, machinery, and small loans. But very soon—and if no malicious intent to exploit one another arises—the fruits will surpass the promises. Moreover, this kind of collaboration that we [PDF 17] request from you is but a local aspect of the same great longing110 that currently stirs the world.Until quite recently, social organization was the work of force, of the soldier or the King. But such [an organizational scheme] was barbaric, and it is being replaced everywhere by republican and more or less socialist forms of government. This requires us to replace the soldier with the person of laws,111 the lawyer or the economist. That is, rather than a government that commands to be obeyed, we have a government of legislators; rather than of the will of the Lord or the king, we have the counsel of citizens. Yet, it is already easy to see that this government of thoughtful people who impose laws, though far superior to the government of the soldier or the King, must itself be surpassed, for it is a means and not an end.Its task is to organize labor, production, and distribution on just foundations. And, consequently, a new form of government, which has already manifested itself occasionally, will have to emerge: the government of the engineer and the technician.112 All the forces of the state will then reconcentrate on extracting nature's treasures and powers. An era—not of industrialism, but of industrialization—will come to pass, in which natural resources will be exploited on a grand scale for the benefit of all people. What industrialism has done for the benefit of the privileged few, the technological industrialization113 of the State shall achieve on a large scale for the common good. And Latin America is precisely the region of the world best suited for the development of this new type of free and industrialized State. To be sure, just as the soldier is replaced by the person of law, and the person of law is replaced by the technician, after the technician will come the period of the philosophers' governance. Production, which will have become an organism set in motion,114 will no longer be the fundamental task. Rather, it will be replaced by education, the task of cultivating and developing spirits.But the government of philosophers—if its mission does not become corrupted—must lead us to a still higher degree of social progress: the disappearance of the State, which too is a means and not an end. For, there is no other end than the individual, the divine spark, the Soul and God, and all else is but straw and vanity. With the disappearance of the State, as having [PDF 18] proved unnecessary, the last trace of barbarism will thus vanish, and all forms of nationalism will be things of the past.We have, then, five stages in the processes of governance, five types of rulers115: the soldier, the lawyer, [p. 24.1] the engineer, the philosopher, and the period that we must call anarchist,116 which is truly the definitive one. But we find ourselves today in the era in which all soldiers should obey the legislators, and when all of us, more or less, must work as engineers and builders. There is so much waste, so much incapacity, and so many unmet needs in the contemporary world that it is indispensable for the period of the engineer to be anticipated and advanced. Work and production are the saving motto—but work and production for the benefit of all who work, without distinction of class or color. All other purposes can wait.

o: [¶ 31] ¿Cuál es nuestra parte, preguntaréis, por último, en toda esta vaga cuestión de los problemas de la América Latina? Vuestra parte puede ser tan importante como la mía o la de cualquiera otro que allá ejerza influencia. La América Latina es una tarea y la tarea pertenece a todo el que pone sobre ella una mano activa y generosa. He ahí por qué no somos extraños unos de otros. Yo vengo de lejos y os hablo en una lengua quenoes la mía ni es tampoco la vuestra; una lengua que no domino, ni me ocuparía tampoco de llegarla a dominar, puesto que como todas las del día, representa tan sólo, una de las maneras imperfectas de expresión del pensamiento; pero nos ha servido para comunicarnos y esto obliga nuestra gratitud; aprendamos de ello hasta qué punto nos hallamos todos los hombres relacionados y unidos.[¶ 32] A causa de mi origen y nombre quizás he despertado lejanos recuerdos en vuestras mentes. Un mexicano tiene que haceros pensar en la historia de Maximiliano, el príncipe infortunado que allá pagó sus errores. Es cierto, nuestras instituciones, nuestras convicciones no nos permitieron, no nos permitirán jamás, así lo espero, recibir a un príncipe como Señor; pero siempre hemos estado dispuestos y seguiremos dispuestos a recibir a cada hombre como un hermano. Los súbditos de los Reyes quedan libres de su voto y sumisión en el instante en que pisan nuestras tierras, así lo dice la Constitución argentina en el extremo sur del continente y así lo confirma la Constitución mexicana en el norte. Procuremos que esta libertad sea efectiva. Desgraciadamente hay muchos esclavos en nuestras tierras; esclavos de situaciones económicas y políticas que sublevan. Pero vosotros podéis ayudarnos con vuestras luces en la cuestión social, con vuestra técnica y vuestra ciencia. Encontraréis por allá empleo para toda clase de facultades. Si queréis una situación estable y de potencialidades ilimitadas, id ala Argentina o al Brasil, a Colombia oa Cuba. Si amáis la fortuna un tanto incierta, preñada quizás de riesgos, pero rica de maravillosas perspectivas, id a mi México. La vida allí se parece a los vinos de la región del Vesubio, jugosos, ardientes y sin igual en el gusto, con algo de espíritu de la tierra inestable, amenazada y fecunda. Escoged vuestra ruta entre los mil caminos del más maravilloso de todos los onctinentes. Por donde quiera que vayáis encontraréis en [p. 24.2] obra dos fuerzas poderosas, dos potencias fascinantes y constructoras: el azar y la fe. Ninguna otra zona del mundo merece con más propiedad el título de país del futuro. Pero vosotros, así como nosotros todos, debemos contribuir a forjar ese futuro. Trabajemos en él, recordando que el presente es siempre el padre de lo que en seguida se vuelve pasado y también de una gran proporción de lo que será el porvenir. De nosotros puede nacer el mañana. Trabajemos juntos para lograr, por lo menos, que el futuro rinda sus mejores, sus más altos frutos.
e: Our civilization will be a failure so long as it continues to produce, like inferior species, more and more people without the means to feed and educate them. Let us ensure that in our America we do not regress into the same errors. We need immigration,117 but without forgetting that before needing many children, we need schools for the children who have already been born. One of the fundamental causes of the lack of prosperity of a civilization lies in the fact that inferior populations reproduce excessively and outnumber advanced ones, which naturally reduce their offspring. For this reason, civilization will only feel secure once culture and true morality, which presuppose responsibility, are propagated among all groups. So long as civilization remains, to a greater or lesser degree, a national matter, there will be no hope for radical changes in the history of the world. Invasions and conquests will continue to produce many more medieval periods, for as long as there are nationalisms, there will be imperialisms and ambitions of conquest; that is, medievalism and barbarism. Civilization, on the contrary, is universality, conscience, and fraternity.What is our part, at last—you may ask—in this vague question of the problems of Latin America? Your part can be as important as mine or that of anyone else who exerts influence there. Latin America is a task, and the task belongs to everyone who lends an active and generous hand to it. That is why we are not strangers to one another. I come from afar and speak to you in a language that is neither yours nor mine, a language that I do not nor bother to [PDF 19] master, since, like all languages of today, it represents only one of the imperfect ways of expressing thought. But it has allowed us to communicate with one other, and for that we owe it gratitude. Let us learn from this how deeply connected and united we all are as human beings.Given my origin and name, perhaps I have awakened distant memories in your minds. A Mexican must remind you of the history of Maximilian, the unfortunate prince who paid for his mistakes in Mexico. It is true, our institutions and conviction did not allow—and I hope never will allow—us to accept a prince as a Lord. But we have always been ready, and will remain ready, to welcome every person as a sibling. The subjects of Kings are freed from their oath and submission the moment they set foot on our soil. This is what the Argentine Constitution declares in the far south of the continent, and this is confirmed by the Mexican Constitution in the north. Let us ensure that this liberty be efficacious.Unfortunately, there are many slaves in our lands, slaves of economic and political conditions that stir outcry.118 But you can help us with your insights into social questions, with your technology119 and your science. You will find there employment for all types of aptitudes. If you seek a stable situation with unlimited potential, go to Argentina or Brazil, to Colombia or Cuba. If you are after a somewhat uncertain fortune, fraught, perhaps, with risks but rich in marvelous prospects, come to my Mexico. Life there resembles the wines of the region of Vesuvius—juicy, fiery, and unparalleled in taste, with something of the spirit of the unstable, threatened, and fertile land. Choose your path among the thousand roads of the most marvelous of all continents.120 Wherever you go, you will find [p. 24.2] two powerful forces at work, two fascinating and constructive powers: chance and faith.121 No other region of the world more rightfully deserves the title of 'the country of the future.' But you, as well as all of us, must contribute to forging that future. Let us work toward it, remembering that the present is always the parent of what soon becomes the past, as well as of a large portion of what will become the future. From us, tomorrow can be born. Let us work together to ensure, at the very least, that the future yields its best, its highest fruits.
